correction: Appended final Remarks only: four-cycle with sole fill edge {v1,v3}, child-to-parent tree v0→v1→v2→v3, C0 and reach comparison. Increased native line width after viewing the first actual dark preview so all edges and arrows are clear.

diagram_math_checks.details: The example is realized by a real symmetric 4×4 matrix with ones on off-diagonal pairs 01,12,23,03 and zeros on other off-diagonal entries. It is Hermitian, and def-hermitian-structural-graph-adapter identifies exactly this four-cycle as its support graph. Vertices are ordered v0,v1,v2,v3.

The supplied elimination definition gives N0(v0)={v1,v3}. Its clique completion adds only {v1,v3}. After deleting v0, the remaining triangle has N1(v1)={v2,v3}, already joined, so no further fill occurs. N2(v2)={v3}, N3(v3)=empty. The assigned definition therefore gives C0={v0,v1,v3} and ell0=2.

The least later neighbor at steps 0,1,2 is respectively v1,v2,v3, so each right-hand arrow has domain child vi and codomain parent v(i+1), for i=0,1,2. v3 is the root. Its chain gives reach(v0)={v0,v1,v2,v3}, with ancestors v1,v2,v3; v2 is in the reach but not C0. No arrow returns to an earlier vertex.

diagram_math_checks.details: The native original-resolution final PNG shows four left vertices and all four solid cycle edges, including explicit v3--v0 closure, plus one dashed fill edge. Their degrees in the displayed filled union are 2,3,2,3. The right tree has four vertices, three arrows and underlying degrees 1,2,2,1. The illustration only explains the existing definitions; no proof or logical premise depends on it.
